writer: an LLM (a research-track sub-agent), from the 68 label names and the public human-rights taxonomy only
reviewer_decision: TEXT_PROCESSING_PLAN.md section 7.1 (CS-11): the catalog is LLM-written, with the writer seeing the label name and the public taxonomy only, never the records
inputs_seen_by_the_writer: the 68 label names (the dataset's own taxonomy terms)
the writer's own knowledge of the public human-rights taxonomy
inputs_never_seen_by_the_writer: any label-frequency statistic (the head / torso / tail / unseen buckets)
any run artifact, any measurement, any val-split number
rules_given_to_the_writer: one short topical description per label, never mentioning frequency
one parent per label, from a single consistent hierarchy of at most 12 categories
the generic labels (General, Other, the two '- general' ones) are described as catch-alls, not as narrow topics
freeze: The catalog is written and committed BEFORE the runs that use it (CS-11's arms and CS-12's listwise question). The sha256 above identifies the frozen version; a later change is a new version, never an edit.
parents: Freedom of expression, association and belief
Liberty and security of the person
The review process, institutions and international framework
note: The catalog is label-side knowledge, the same kind of thing the zero-shot label vectors are allowed to use. It is not part of the dataset and never changes the raw data (AGENTS.md: the raw data is read-only).
